comparison: Perfect alignment on safety data (C22, C31-C34, C70). Both evaluations find the safety reporting well-supported with adequate documentation. OpenEval emphasizes transparent reporting of specific frequencies and grades, while peer reviewers accepted safety findings without challenge as part of 'high-quality data'.

Strong agreement on diarrhea management discussion (C46-C49, C60, C63). Both find the loperamide prophylaxis discussion and consistency with prior studies well-supported. OpenEval highlights appropriate external evidence citation, while peer reviewers accepted the safety discussion but requested more comprehensive literature review on pyrotinib combinations.

Strong agreement on core study design and baseline characteristics (C10-C12, C23-C29, C66-C69, C82). Both evaluations find these claims well-supported. OpenEval notes internal consistency and clear documentation, while peer reviewers praised 'robust logic and high-quality data' from the multicenter design. OpenEval covers additional claims (C74-C78, C82-C84) not explicitly mentioned in peer review.

Agreement on primary efficacy results (C13, C30). Both find the iDFS data supported. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate statistical reporting with confidence intervals and visual confirmation via Kaplan-Meier curves. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as 'fully supported' without concerns about primary efficacy results.

Agreement on background literature and epidemiological context (C1-C6, C51-C52). Both evaluations find these claims accurately represent established data with appropriate citations. OpenEval validates consistency with current knowledge, while peer reviewers accepted the background but suggested it could be more comprehensive.

Agreement on pyrotinib mechanism and prior evidence (C7-C9). Both find these claims appropriately cited and valid. OpenEval confirms accurate description of mechanism and clinical evidence, while peer reviewers accepted this rationale without challenge.

Significant disagreement on treatment duration subgroup analysis (C14, C15). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to overlapping confidence intervals, small sample size (n=31 in 6-month group), and lack of statistical comparison. Peer reviewers rated as SUPPORTED, accepting the subgroup analyses without questioning the limitations.

Disagreement on HR status subgroup analysis (C16, C17). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the numerical difference lacks statistical testing and mechanistic explanation is speculative. Peer reviewers rated as SUPPORTED, accepting subgroup results without challenge. OpenEval also addresses mechanistic claims (C37, C38, C73) not evaluated separately by peer reviewers.

Disagreement on nodal status subgroup analysis (C18, C19). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to overlapping confidence intervals, wide CI for node-negative patients (n=34), and lack of statistical comparison. Peer reviewers rated as SUPPORTED, accepting the subgroup data without questioning precision limitations.

Disagreement on trastuzumab use subgroup analysis (C20, C21). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting overlapping confidence intervals, lack of statistical testing, and speculative interpretation about dual blockade benefits. Peer reviewers rated as SUPPORTED, accepting these subgroup findings. OpenEval also addresses related discussion claims (C41, C55, C72) about APHINITY extrapolation.

Major disagreement on comparative efficacy claims (C35, C36). OpenEval rates as UNSUPPORTED, identifying methodologically flawed comparison between single-arm PERSIST and randomized ExteNET treatment arm without proper controls. Peer reviewers rated as SUPPORTED, accepting the comparative interpretation and novelty claim without challenging the comparison methodology.

Disagreement on novelty and conclusion claims (C54, C64, C65). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting 'promising efficacy' is limited by single-arm design, short follow-up, high discontinuation rate, and lack of control group. Peer reviewers rated as SUPPORTED, accepting the novelty claim and acknowledging it 'introduces a novel therapeutic strategy' while requesting more detailed description.

Agreement on statistical planning (C79-C81). Both find the statistical methodology acceptable. OpenEval notes transparent planning with appropriate justification and acknowledges actual dropout exceeded planned rate. Peer reviewers accepted methodology but requested clarification on data distribution and statistical analysis expansion.

Agreement on background clinical trial context (C39, C40). Both evaluations find these established trial results appropriately cited. OpenEval confirms accurate representation supporting treatment duration rationale, while peer reviewers accepted this contextual discussion without challenge.

Partial agreement on regulatory context and speculation (C42-C44, C71). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, accepting factual regulatory claims but noting speculation about benefit after T-DM1 extrapolates from metastatic to adjuvant setting without evidence. Peer reviewers rated as SUPPORTED, accepting the discussion framework but requesting expansion.

Agreement on regulatory and guideline context (C56-C59). Both evaluations find these factual claims about regulatory status and standards of care well-supported. OpenEval confirms verifiable facts supporting clinical relevance, while peer reviewers accepted this contextual information without challenge.

Agreement on trial registration and limitation acknowledgment (C50, C61). Both find transparent acknowledgment of high discontinuation rate appropriate. OpenEval emphasizes recognition of study weaknesses, while peer reviewers accepted the limitation disclosure as part of acceptable methodology.

Agreement on mechanistic hypothesis (C62). Both evaluations find the cautious presentation of the 'mainstream hypothesis' appropriate. OpenEval notes proper acknowledgment of uncertainty, while peer reviewers accepted this discussion without challenge.

Disagreement on mechanistic interpretation (C37, C38, C73). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanistic explanation is speculative and based on neratinib preclinical data rather than pyrotinib, with unquantified confounding from endocrine therapy. Peer reviewers rated as SUPPORTED, accepting the mechanistic framework and treatment protocol without questioning the speculative nature.

Partial overlap on dual blockade discussion (C41, C55, C72). OpenEval rates interpretation as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about persistent dual blockade benefits based on APHINITY rather than demonstrated in this study. Peer reviewers accepted the contextual discussion framework as SUPPORTED but requested expansion.
